statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail stands at 11 of 100 in the low band, fourteen points below the 25 block threshold, while stress is extreme at 86 and confidence high at 88.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. The named danger window spans the 12:30 UTC August consumer price report, the 13:30 UTC cash open and the 14:00 UTC preliminary Michigan release, where the conditional path peaks at WATCH without reaching the block threshold.
headline: NQ trades 29,149.50, up 0.05%, after fully retracing the 29,042.00 overnight low without extending the 29,171.50 high, which eases tail to 11, while a 4.944% ten-year, Brent near $107 and a September rate increase priced near 71% keep stress extreme at 86 into the August consumer price report.
body:
The new evidence this hour is the completion of a full two-way rotation of the overnight range. NQ trades 29,149.50, up 14.25 points or 0.05%, against a band of 29,042.00 to 29,171.50. An hour ago price stood at 29,085.75 and had just probed the low; it has since recovered roughly 108 points from that low and now sits within 22 points of the session high without extending it. A second independent quote source reports 29,164.25 with the same band intact, so both the recovery and the unbroken high are confirmed on two feeds.

That sequence is what lowers tail a point to 11. Tail measures a persistent no-retracement price path, not direction and not proximity to an extreme. A low that is probed, fully bought back, and followed by an approach to the opposite edge that also stalls is the signature of a market rotating between two accepted boundaries. The overnight session has now visited both edges of a 129.5-point band and held neither, which is the opposite of repeated extension after failed retracements. None of the amplifiers that would justify a higher reading are present in the observed path: there is no shallow-pullback sequence, no session extreme that price is pinning, and no one-way structure.

The macro backdrop is unchanged and remains severe, which is why stress holds at 86 in the extreme band. The ten-year Treasury yield closed at 4.944%, up 10.7 basis points on the day and the highest since 2023, after a day range of 4.879% to 4.952%. The most recent Federal Reserve H.15 publication shows the two-year at 4.43% and the ten-year at 4.83% as of 9 September, so the curve has repriced materially since that release. Brent trades near $106.90 and WTI near $101.97, both easing modestly on the day but still on course for a weekly gain above 12% on Middle East supply risk. The VIX closed at 17.84, up 8.4%. The Nasdaq 100 cash index closed at 29,103.51, down 1.08%, its fourth consecutive decline.

The session's defining checkpoint is the August consumer price report at 12:30 UTC, the last inflation reading before the 16 September policy decision. Consensus is 3.4% headline and 2.4% core year over year, with energy pass-through the main upside channel, and futures pricing places a quarter-point rate increase at roughly 71%. Under the prior calibration, event importance and forecast dispersion raise stress and lower confidence rather than raising tail before anything prints. The forward path therefore peaks at a conditional tail of 23 in the release hour and 22 across the cash open, both inside the watch band and below the 25 block threshold.

Confidence holds at 88. Price, band, yields, oil, volatility and the calendar are each verified against primary or reputable current sources, and the two futures feeds agree to within fifteen points. The shared cross-asset context file carries a collection timestamp of 01:31 UTC and a partial collection status, which places it outside the ninety-minute freshness limit, so it was treated as stale and this assessment rests entirely on independent research.

lookbackSummary: All 24 clock-hours from 05:00 UTC on 10 September to 04:00 UTC on 11 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens at tail 10 and holds a 9 to 11 band through the European morning, with the dominant mode recorded as mixed throughout. The regime change sits in the middle of the U.S. session: tail 14 at 11:00 UTC as the mode turned trend-down on the pre-release grind, 20 at 12:00 UTC when the August producer price report printed and the mode became event/whipsaw, and the window peak of 24 at 13:00 UTC across the cash open, the only two slots mapped to WATCH. Tail then decayed as price discovery stayed orderly, easing to 17 by 14:00 UTC and holding 14 to 19 through the afternoon, with event/whipsaw recorded again from 19:00 to 21:00 UTC around the cash close. From the 22:00 UTC reopen the series settles back into a mixed 11 to 15 range, ending at 12 for the two hours before this assessment. Stress never left the extreme band, running 80 to 87 across the whole window, and confidence stayed in the high band between 84 and 89. The shape of the window is therefore a single event-driven excursion into the watch band that fully reverted, not a sustained escalation.
outlookSummary: The forward window opens with about five hours of observed post-reopen trade on 11 September, covers the full U.S. session, and then ends inside the CME weekend closure that begins at 21:00 UTC. Conditional tail starts at 11, holds 11 through the thinnest pre-European hour, and rebuilds gradually from the European cash open, 12 through 14, reaching 16 in the final full hour before the release as quoted depth conditionally thins. The window peak is 23 in the 12:00 UTC slot containing the August consumer price report, which stays inside the watch band and below the 25 block threshold, and 22 in the 13:00 UTC slot spanning the cash open, where a post-event move is most often confirmed or rejected. The 14:00 UTC slot carrying the preliminary Michigan release eases to 19 on the assumption that price discovery is orderly by then. The afternoon decays through 17, 15 and 14, lifts to 15 into the final cash hour and 18 across the 20:00 UTC close where weekend positioning concentrates, then collapses to a 5 to 6 floor for the eight closure hours in which no tradeable price path exists. Stress mirrors that shape, peaking at 92 in the release hour and falling to 61 inside the closure, while confidence dips to 80 around the release and to 81 late in the weekend as the last observed price path ages. Two slots map to WATCH and the remaining twenty-two map to EA_ON.
